figures.finding: Honduras's Ley de Cinematografía (approved by Congress on 30 January 2019) created a film directorate (DGC), a national film council and a film development fund (FONDECI), reported at L40 million and aimed mainly at training, promotion and specific projects, with a 100% income-tax credit for investment in features capped at US$100,000 for large taxpayers and US$50,000 for small and medium ones.
figures.applies: Honduras, as the press reported the law in 2019; the fund's 2026 budget, calls and selection rate were not found (the IAIP transparency portal's copy of the draft regulation answered 403, cultura.gob.hn CONNECT 502).

sources.said: La ley cuenta con un fondo de 40 millones de lempiras enfocado principalmente a la formación, promoción y proyectos específicos. El gobernante detalló que se establece el 100% del incentivo fiscal del Impuesto Sobre la Renta (ISR) a personas naturales o jurídicas para proyectos de largometrajes con límite de 100.000 dólares para grandes contribuyentes y 50.000 dólares para pequeños y medianos.

On January 30, 2019, the Honduran National Congress approved the law passed down by the Executive Branch. … 3. The fund for film development will be created (FONDECI). … 4. Tax incentives will be created for national film investment.
